title: AI & Technology Risk Auditor - Lead Consultant
description: At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. Your role in the team Internal Audit provides independent assurance and advisory services that help Allstate manage risk, strengthen controls, and improve business performance. As emerging technologies transform the organization, Internal Audit plays a critical role in evaluating the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and control frameworks across technology, data, and AI-enabled solutions. The Lead AI & Technology Risk Auditor is a senior audit professional responsible for leading complex technology and business audits across high-risk and emerging technology domains, with a particular focus on Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative AI, Machine Learning (ML), advanced analytics platforms, and cloud-native technologies. This role serves as both an audit leader and subject matter expert, designing and executing audit strategies that evaluate the effectiveness of technology controls, AI governance practices, model risk management, automation frameworks, and data-driven decision-making systems. The Lead AI & Technology Risk Auditor provides independent assurance over AI-enabled solutions while helping the audit function evolve through the adoption of AI-assisted auditing techniques, data analytics, automation, and innovative audit methodologies. Working closely with business leaders, technology partners, risk functions, and audit teams, this individual influences audit strategy, mentors auditors, and helps ensure that Allstate's adoption of AI technologies remains secure, compliant, ethical, and appropriately governed. Key Responsibilities: Independently lead complex technology, cyber, data, and AI-focused audits from planning through reporting, ensuring delivery of high-quality audit outcomes within agreed timelines. Develop and execute risk-based audit programs that assess governance, risk management, and control effectiveness across technology platforms, cloud environments, AI systems, and data solutions. Evaluate controls supporting the design, development, deployment, monitoring, and ongoing governance of AI and machine learning solutions. Assess generative AI and large language model (LLM) implementations, including model governance, prompt engineering controls, output validation processes, data privacy protections, and third-party AI service provider oversight. Apply data analytics, automation, and AI-assisted audit techniques to improve audit effectiveness, perform full-population testing, identify anomalies, and uncover emerging risks. Conduct walkthroughs, control assessments, testing procedures, and root cause analysis for complex technology and business processes. Communicate audit observations and recommendations through sprint reviews, stakeholder discussions, and formal audit reports. Partner with technology and business leaders to understand strategic initiatives, emerging risks, and evolving regulatory requirements. Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical guidance to audit team members in areas including technology risk, AI governance, data analytics, control evaluation, and strategic thinking. Contribute to Internal Audit transformation initiatives through the development of innovative audit methodologies, AI-enabled audit practices, continuous monitoring capabilities, and automation solutions. Maintain awareness of emerging AI regulations, industry standards, and technology trends, incorporating them into audit planning and execution. Essential Skills: All applicants must demonstrate they have a legal right to work in the UK for employment at Allstate. Allstate is not providing sponsorship for this vacancy. A minimum of 4 years of experience in Internal Audit, External Audit, Risk Management, Technology Risk, Cybersecurity, or Technology Control functions within a regulated or large enterprise environment. A minimum of 1 year of professional experience auditing, implementing, assessing, governing, or supporting AI, Machine Learning, Generative AI, or Advanced Analytics solutions. Practical experience with at least one analytical or technical tool such as Python, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Alteryx, SAS, or equivalent. Proven experience presenting audit findings, risk assessments, or technology control recommendations to senior management and business stakeholders. Desirable Skills: Professional certification including CISA, CIA, CPA, CFE, CA, CRISC, CISSP, or equivalent. AI-related certifications such as: ISACA AI Fundamentals ISACA Advanced in AI Audit (AAIA) AWS AI Certifications Microsoft Azure AI Certifications Data Science or Machine Learning certificatio

title: Lead Program Manager, Finance Transformation
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role Veeam's Finance Transformation Office (FTO) is looking for a highly organized and execution-focused Lead Program Manager to drive strategic Finance transformation initiatives across the organization. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in complex, cross-functional environments and enjoys connecting Finance, Corporate Technology, and implementation partners to deliver meaningful business outcomes. As a Lead Program Manager, you will own the day-to-day execution of one or more transformation programs, ensuring projects remain on track, risks are proactively managed, and executive stakeholders have clear visibility into progress, dependencies, and business value. You'll serve as the operational backbone of the program, helping Finance leaders successfully deliver large-scale initiatives that modernize systems, processes, and reporting capabilities. This role reports into the Finance Transformation Office Governance & Process Architecture team and requires a combination of program management expertise, financial systems knowledge, strong executive communication, and the ability to influence stakeholders across multiple organizations. What You'll Do Lead the execution of one or more Finance Transformation initiatives, driving timelines, milestones, deliverables, and cross-functional coordination. Build and maintain program governance, including executive status reporting, steering committee materials, RAID logs, and portfolio dashboards. Identify, track, and proactively manage risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies across Finance, Corporate Technology, and external implementation partners. Partner with Functional Transformation Leads across FP&A, Controllership, Treasury, Tax, and other Finance organizations to ensure business requirements remain aligned throughout delivery. Collaborate with Corporate Technology teams and System Integrators to support successful implementation of Finance systems, data platforms, and enterprise applications. Monitor program health, benefit realization, and strategic outcomes, ensuring initiatives deliver measurable business value beyond project completion. Support organizational change management activities by partnering on communication plans, training, adoption strategies, and stakeholder engagement. Facilitate governance meetings, executive reviews, decision-making sessions, and cross-functional workshops with senior leadership. Drive continuous improvement by standardizing governance processes, templates, reporting frameworks, and program management best practices across the Finance Transformation Office. Foster collaboration, accountability, and transparency across all program stakeholders while maintaining focus on delivery excellence. What You'll Bring Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field. 5+ years of program or project management experience delivering Finance Transformation, ERP, Enterprise Planning, or Data Platform initiatives within complex, matrixed organizations. Experience managing enterprise implementations involving platforms such as Oracle Cloud ERP, SAP, NetSuite, Pigment, Anaplan, Adaptive Planning, Databricks, Snowflake, or similar technologies. Strong knowledge of project governance methodologies, including RAID management, RACI/DACI frameworks, executive reporting, and portfolio governance. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple cross-functional initiatives while balancing competing priorities and executive expectations. Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with a proactive approach to risk management. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English, with experience presenting program updates and recommendations to senior leadership. Experience working collaboratively with Finance organizations, Corporate Technology teams, and third-party implementation partners. Ability to operate effectively in fast-paced environments with evolving priorities and ambiguous requirements. Nice to Have PMP, PRINCE2, PMI-ACP, Scrum Master, or equivalent project management certification. Experience supporting Finance organizations through digital transformation or enterprise modernization initiatives. Exposure to SOX controls, audit readiness, or IPO environments. title: Senior Manager - Data & AI Governance
description: Mercury is seeking a Data & AI Governance leader to build and spearhead an enterprise-wide governance program for data and artificial intelligence. Reporting to the Chief Risk Officer, this leader will establish practical standards for how data and AI are owned, developed, used, protected, and monitored across the organization. The ideal candidate combines strong governance and risk-management experience with sufficient technical fluency to work effectively with Data, Engineering, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams. This person should be comfortable building in a fast-moving environment and designing governance that supports responsible innovation without creating unnecessary complexity. This role will work closely with the Model Risk Management and Information Security teams while maintaining a distinct mandate: Data & AI Governance will establish enterprise governance and responsible-use standards, while Model Risk Management will retain responsibility for model inventory, tiering, validation, and model-risk oversight. Key Responsibilities: Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise Data and AI Governance frameworks, policies, standards, and operating model. Establish clear accountability for data ownership, stewardship, quality, lineage, classification, access, retention, and appropriate use. Create a risk-based governance process for AI use cases across their lifecycle, including intake, assessment, approval, implementation, monitoring, and retirement. Develop responsible-AI principles and standards addressing transparency, explainability, fairness, privacy, security, human oversight, reliability, and regulatory compliance. Maintain an enterprise inventory of material data assets, AI use cases, and related governance decisions in coordination with relevant stakeholders. Define risk-based classifications and governance requirements based on the sensitivity, complexity, materiality, and customer or regulatory impact of each use case. Establish governance for internally developed, vendor-provided, and embedded AI capabilities, including generative AI. Partner with various Product, Engineering, Data, and business teams to embed governance requirements into development and change-management processes. Coordinate with Model Risk Management to determine when an AI use case meets the definition of a model and is subject to model-risk requirements. Partner with Information Security and Technology Risk on data protection, cybersecurity, access, architecture, resilience, and technology-control considerations. Partner with Legal and Compliance to identify and implement applicable regulatory, contractual, consumer-protection, and privacy requirements. Develop processes for identifying, documenting, escalating, and remediating data- and AI-related risks and issues. Establish metrics/reporting to provide management and Board committees with visibility into data quality, governance maturity, AI adoption, exceptions, incidents, and emerging risks. Monitor regulatory developments, industry practices, and emerging risks related to data and AI, and translate them into proportionate governance expectations. Support relevant Data and AI governance forums/committees and facilitate timely, well-documented decisions. Eventually, build and lead a high-performing Data & AI Governance team as the program matures. Promote a culture in which data is treated as an enterprise asset and AI is used responsibly, transparently, and in alignment with Mercury’s risk appetite. Qualifications: 10+ years of relevant experience in data governance, AI governance, technology risk, information governance, model risk, privacy, compliance, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing a data governance, AI governance, or responsible-AI program. Strong understanding of data ownership, stewardship, quality, lineage, metadata, classification, access, retention, and lifecycle management. Working knowledge of AI and machine-learning concepts, including generative AI, large language models, training and inference data, explainability, bias, performance monitoring, and human oversight. Experience developing practical, risk-based policies and governance processes that can operate effectively in a fast-moving technology environment. Ability to distinguish among data governance, AI governance, model risk, information security, privacy, and compliance responsibilities while coordinating effectively across those functions. Strong judgment and the ability to balance innovation, customer outcomes, regulatory expectations, and risk management. Demonstrated ability to influence senior executives, technical teams, and business leaders without relying solely on formal authority. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical and risk concepts to executive and Board audiences. title: Managing Principal Consultant – Life & Pensions
description: Managing Principal Consultant – Life & Pensions Location: London (Hybrid) | Practice Area: Insurance, Business Consulting | Type: Permanent Help shape the future of Life & Pensions through strategic transformation and innovation. The Role We are looking for a Managing Principal Consultant with deep Life & Pensions expertise to support and deliver high-impact projects for our UK clients. This role blends strategic leadership, delivery, and hands-on consulting across digital transformation, data, regulatory change, customer transformation, and AI-enabled business transformation. You'll collaborate closely with clients and internal teams to align business and technology priorities while helping expand Capco's Life & Pensions consulting practice. You'll also encourage the responsible use of approved AI tools and AI-enabled workflows to improve delivery quality, accelerate insight, and enhance client outcomes, applying appropriate human judgement and governance throughout. What You'll Do Deliver complex change and transformation programmes across the Life & Pensions sector, using AI-enabled approaches where appropriate to improve efficiency, insight, and delivery quality. Support initiatives across digital transformation, customer experience, data, regulatory change, AI, and agile ways of working. Engage senior client stakeholders, coordinate multidisciplinary teams, and ensure successful value delivery, embedding responsible AI practices and appropriate governance throughout delivery. Support business development activities, contributing to client growth and account development, including identifying opportunities where AI can create measurable business value. Build trusted partnerships with clients, vendors, and internal stakeholders across business and technology domains, encouraging practical adoption of AI-enabled ways of working aligned to client objectives. What We're Looking For Proven experience of consultancy within the Life & Pensions sector. Strong track record delivering large-scale transformation programmes and complex change initiatives. Deep knowledge of Life & Pensions operations, including policy administration, customer servicing, digital enablement, data governance, target operating model design, and an understanding of how AI can enhance business and technology transformation. Excellent stakeholder management, influencing, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to support senior leaders in the responsible adoption of AI where appropriate. Experience of generating revenue within a consulting environment, while developing and managing senior client relationships, along with curiosity to explore approved AI tools and automation to improve delivery, productivity, and insight. Bonus Points For Experience supporting agile transformation initiatives and product ownership. Strong knowledge of UK Life & Pensions regulation and change programmes, including awareness of AI governance and regulatory considerations. Experience designing and implementing target operating models that incorporate AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate. An established professional network with experience developing new client opportunities within the Life & Pensions market. Experience using or advising on AI (including Generative AI or Agentic AI), automation, or AI-enabled workflows within Financial Services organisations. Why Join Capco Deliver strategic transformation programmes for leading global financial institutions. Work in a collaborative, flat, and entrepreneurial consulting environment where your ideas and expertise make a real difference. Access continuous learning, professional development, and industry-recognised certifications to support your career growth. Build your career alongside experts in strategy, transformation and financial services. Help shape the future of transformation across Financial Services through innovation, digital capabilities, and AI-enabled ways of working. Benefits We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life: Core Benefits: Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover. Mental Health: Easy access to CareFirst, Unmind, Aviva consultations, and in-house first aiders. Family-Friendly: Maternity, adoption, shared parental leave, plus paid leave for sickness, pregnancy loss, fertility treatment, menopause, and bereavement. Family Care: Eight complimentary backup care sessions for emergency childcare or elder care. Holiday Flexibility: Five weeks of annual leave with the option to buy or sell holiday days based on your needs. Continuous Learning: Your growth, your way – minimum 40 hours of training annually through workshops, certifications and e-learning. You'll also be assigned a Business Coach from Day One to provide one-to-one guidance and accelerate your development. Healthcare Access: Convenient online GP services. Extra Perks: Gympass (Wellhub), travel insurance, Tastecard, season ticket loans, Cycle to Work, and dental insurance.
